newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale seen ruling on emergency harvest fund soon.
newsitem.headline: Goodale seen ruling on emergency harvest fund soon.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale will likely decide next week whether to approve emergency funds to farmers in the northwest Prairies who were not able to harvest their wheat or barley due to cold, wet conditions, the minister's spokesman said.

"It's among a package of materials for Ralph to look at when he comes back from Rome tonight. I expect he'll make a decision early next week once he talks to the (Canadian Wheat) Board to find out how much grain was left standing on the 15th," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
By law the funds cannot be approved before Nov 15.
Goodale was in Rome this week for a United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization meeting.
The CWB and Alberta's agriculture minister asked Goodale to approve the funds which would allow payments of up to C$15,000 a farmer for unharvested wheat and barley and C$3,000 a farmer to dry grain.
The emergency fund was last invoked in 1993, the CWB said.
"I don't expect he'll be saying anything about it until Monday at the earliest," Greenshields added.
